title: Titanium Waterjet Impeller
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this propulsion application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by waterjet propulsion inducer impeller and specific design requirements.
process: Ring forging radial-axial for propulsion geometry
CNC turn-bore operation with SPC sampling
TIG welding autogenous with SPC sampling
Hydrostatic pressure test with SPC sampling
surfaceTreatment: Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater — tailored for waterjet propulsion inducer application
commonFailures: Crevice corrosion under biofouling in stagnant seawater - mitigated by CP-Ti Grade 2 + ICCP system — critical for waterjet propulsion inducer performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Waterjet Impeller suitable for Waterjet propulsion inducer impeller?
faq.a: Titanium Waterjet Impeller uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address propulsion operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Waterjet Impeller?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Waterjet Impeller is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for waterjet propulsion inducer requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Waterjet Impeller require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. waterjet propulsion inducer components require Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater — tailored for waterjet propulsion inducer application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Waterjet Impeller shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Waterjet Impeller includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet waterjet propulsion inducer specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
